question: Does coyote (Canis latrans) versus bobcat (Lynx rufus) observed NIGHT−DAY GPS displacement q ordering, and q~daylength seasonal slope difference, recur across two original Illinois and Washington studies when both taxa are observed on the same astronomy-qualified source calendar days?

source_studies.file_name: GPS tracking of bobcats and coyotes in northern Washington.csv

source_integrity: Exact pre-existing public source UUID, file size, original provider MD5 and old original solar-heading source total/native rows, hour-selected fixes and native tag counts required before new q effect. Both source GPS files were already opened for solar-direction analysis; this new q slope is post-source but before temporal effect sign inspection.
native_unit: One independently published Movebank study DOI, with species nested inside study. Two source studies not four independent ecosystems. Illinois white-tailed deer native taxon stays in full result even when not part of target coyote/bobcat contrast.
original_hourbin: One fix per UTC-hour bin selected only by timestamp; accepted actual 0.5 to 2 hour consecutive GPS straight-line intervals, speed at most 60 km/h, same astronomical solar date/part at start/mid/end. At least three day and three night GPS steps per animal-day, ten qualifying days/year.
source_shared_dates: Within each study coyote and bobcat must both have at least one tagged animal eligible on identical source astronomy calendar date; source date support chosen by iterative fixed-point 10-day-per-tag-year and 0.5h seasonal range rules without peeking at q or effect signs.
astronomy_reference: 43.0 degrees N reference astronomical daylength for the same native source calendar dates, following previous Utah/Wyoming two-study comparison; not the physical local photoperiod of the original GPS site.
source_q: Mean tag-level observed NIGHT−DAY q = log1p(median nighttime straight-line GPS displacement km/h)−log1p(median daytime speed km/h) on source-shared dates.
source_daylength: Within-tag/calendar-year OLS of daily q versus common 43N source astronomical daylength (>=0.5h range), equal years within tag. Primary inference tag-block bootstrap; secondary datewise q difference versus daylength year-month block bootstrap.
three_observation_schedules: Original UTC-hourbin source primary; even and odd UTC-hour bin alternate 2h source only as support-qualified secondary if both native species qualify for same date support. No replacement/relaxation if 2h lacks enough day/night source steps.
bootstrap: Source original tagged individuals >=5 per taxon, 2000 deterministic original tag resamples for coyote-minus-bobcat q and q~daylength; year-month blocks >=5 and common days>=20 for date-level slope. All intervals descriptive unadjusted multiple comparisons.
missingness: If a taxon/source cannot support shared calendar, source stays HOLD/UNAVAILABLE not an ecological zero. Both source DOIs and all 5 original source×taxon groups preserved regardless of outcome.
privacy: Do not export original tag IDs, true site/grid, exact original calendar dates, event times/positions, per-tag parameters or raw tracking payloads.
old_results: The prior Utah/Wyoming two-species diel rank result, historical 12 ERA5 raw-JSON source holds and previously preregistered 48 source negative-direction shortwave nonreplication remain unmodified.
